title: Kaleidoscope: Precise Invariant-Guided Pointer Analysis
problem: Pointer analysis techniques suffer from imprecision, reporting points-to sets that are supersets of actual runtime points-to sets. This false imprecision limits the effectiveness of security mitigations that depend on precise pointer information.
motivation: Precise pointer analysis is essential for implementing effective software security mitigations including control flow integrity and other defenses.
method: Kaleidoscope performs static analysis by making optimistic assumptions: it predicts that pointers point to a narrower set of locations than standard analysis would allow. During program execution, it validates these predictions by checking if pointers actually behave as assumed. When validation succeeds, the precise predictions are used; when validation fails, it falls back to a conservative standard analysis that guarantees correctness.
key_novelty: Verifying optimistic pointer predictions at runtime and falling back to guaranteed-correct analysis when predictions prove wrong.
contributions: 13.15× reduction in average points-to set size over state-of-the-art frameworks
Invariant-guided optimistic pointer analysis technique with runtime verification
Enhanced control flow integrity implementation using precise pointer analysis
